sentences.text: Researchers developed a computational model identifying four distinct chloride trajectories using 1,817 patients from one database, then validated these patterns against 1,154 patients from a second dataset.
The identified trajectories were categorized as low and stable, mid and stable, high and rising, and very high with a rise and plateau.
In the initial cohort, patients exhibiting low-stable, high-rising, or very-high rise/plateau patterns showed higher in-hospital mortality than those with the mid-stable profile.
However, these mortality associations were not statistically significant in the second database, and no clear link emerged between the chloride patterns and acute kidney injury in either group.
The authors suggest that while these patterns appear identifiable across different hospitals, their predictive value for death requires further external testing before clinical application.
